賽事頭廿分鐘，雙方已踢得頗有火藥味，直至「水Break」後，雙方各有球員領黃牌，分別為英格蘭中場安達臣（Elliot Anderson）、阿根廷中堅利辛度馬天尼斯（Lisandro Martínez）；上半場為止，幾乎每響一下哨音，球迷即為愛隊歡呼，也為對方犯規動作喝倒采。

雙方上半場打和，但下半場換邊後，第 55 分鐘，英格蘭哥頓（Anthony Gordon）接應，率先攻破阿根廷大門，領先 1 比 0，全場英格蘭球迷馬上歡呼慶祝。

阿根廷被先開記錄後即奮起直追，10 分鐘內三度從右路傳中組織攻勢，均被擋出，讓不少阿根廷球迷嘆氣。直至第 85 分鐘，安素費蘭南斯（Enzo Fernández）接獲美斯傳球頂入，為阿根廷追和 1 比 1，阿根廷球迷即狂歡、擊鼓、吹響喇叭。

補時階段第 92 分鐘，美斯助攻，由拿達路馬天尼斯（Lautaro Martínez）絕殺英格蘭，再次晉身決賽，與西班牙爭奪大力神盃。全場阿根廷球迷再次陷入瘋狂，當完場哨聲一響，球迷繼續相擁狂歡，有人更將商場的美斯紙牌舉起慶祝。

阿根廷球迷阿豪指，從美斯於巴塞隆拿出道時已是其球迷。身穿「兩星」阿根廷 10 號球衣的他說，今屆是美斯最後一屆世界盃，同時挑戰衛冕。偶像美斯與球隊於今屆賽事掀起爭論，阿豪認為，與其執拗每場執法呎度，倒不如珍惜美斯最後效力國家隊的時光。他又笑言，「趁後生仲頂到」，選擇捱夜到商場與其他球迷同樂，氣氛更勝在家睇波，最終結果亦如他所願，阿根廷晉身決賽。

英格蘭球迷於今屆賽事高呼「Football’s coming home！」未能再下一城，把足球帶回家。在英國留學的 Declan，趁著暑假回港。今日他披英格蘭國旗，在兩隊激鬥之際，與同行友人全情打氣。他說，今次是首次到商場觀賽體驗氣氛，認為球迷有激情，但同時各自尊重，不會有過激衝突。

愛隊落敗，球迷難免失落，與中場迪勤懷斯（Declan Rice）同名的 Declan 認為，今仗英格蘭表現已經不錯，自己也是兩屆球迷，直言「都等咗 60 年，等多四年都無乜嘢！」

阿根廷將在 20 日對西班牙爭取衛冕，季軍之戰，英格蘭會在 19 日對法國。

居民代表大律師陳詞：有持份者想卸責

大律師譚俊傑代表九位居民包括八名遺屬陳詞，指火災因一環接一環的涉事方失誤或意外而發生，並重整聽證會的證據，逐一分析涉事方角色，包括大維修總承建商宏業、工程顧問鴻毅及註冊檢驗人員吳躍、中華發展工程、宏泰消防工程、置邦興業有限公司、房屋局獨立審查組、屋宇署、勞工署、消防處、市建局；另於書面陳詞分析法團前主席鄧國權、法團前顧問兼大埔區議員黃碧嬌的角色。

譚俊傑代表九位居民分別為李國鴻、羅曉琪、羅曉健、葉家駒、葉信霆、葉信賢、蘇曉峯、鍾小碧及江祥，講述總結陳詞。

譚俊傑指，大火於去年11月發生，由三月開始聽證會以來，許多居民強忍悲痛作供，他指，部分人親歷其境，「全部都是我難以想像的痛」。他指，聽證會內，部分證人只是想推卸責任，「我明白他們（災民）為何會忍不住有怒火」，他指這樣推卸責任，對委員會、整個香港尋找今次事件真相沒有幫助。

政府陳詞：多名持份者持續蓄意違法

政府陳詞分八部分，包括政府的立場、監管架構、大火起因、有關專業人士系統性機制濫用、救火救援工作檢視、規管架構弱點和可改善的地方等。政府在陳詞中，將火災形容為「多名持份者在一段時間內持續作出多方面的蓄意違法行為」、而非「單一制度弱點」的結果。

委員會今早上載政府陳詞及摘要，當中提到在如私人建築物管理及業主委聘專業人士範疇中，政府的角色屬促進及推動性質；在如消防風險管理、施工物料規管及職業安全範疇，政府則擔當監督角色。

陳詞指，火災並非單一疏忽或單一制度弱點的結果，而是「多名持份者在一段時間內持續作出多方面的蓄意違法行為」所致，負有首要責任的專業人士及其他私營持份者蓄意欺瞞和敷衍塞責。

政府在陳詞指，火災的每一項促成因素，均可追溯至該持份者的作為或不作為，有關違法行為刻意規避及破壞現有制度框架，嚴重阻礙及削弱政府的監管職能。陳詞又指出，多個現行制度的「系統性弱點」，包括制度設計在面對「蓄意合謀或完全怠忽職守之情況」時，不足以揭示違法行為；以統計抽樣為基礎的審核機制不足以偵測蓄意和有組織的隱瞞；程序指引及工作守則「存在改善空間」、屋宇署與ICU之間溝通機制有「弱點」、以及科技應用滯後。

代表政府的資深大律師孫靖乾表示，對於委員會不向行政長官請求將調查轉為法定性質，政府理解及尊重其決定，即使有部分涉事者，尤其宏業鴻毅拒絕且沒有參與聽證會作供，委員會都可以透過書面供詞及資料作相關事實裁斷，即使涉事方放棄在公眾面前解釋的機會，委員會都可以對他們作出裁斷，甚至是對該方不利的裁斷。

「將焦點針對政府屬偏頗」

孫續指，政府理解社會各界將焦點放在各作供的政府部門，「但如果社會因此忽略其他涉事方，包括沒有出席聽證會的涉事方的責任，甚至將焦點全部聚焦或針對政府，甚至認為有關部門是大火始作俑者，則難免有所偏頗，無論對政府還是公眾利益，這種觀感屬片面、不公平」。他重申，政府並非迴避監督或監管責任，惟有傳媒報道將火災責任完全歸咎政府，「認為是因為政府部門最終鑄成大錯，姑勿論是否事實，這樣寫法將兩層責任混為一談，將系統、執行弱點變成火警直接成因，是不符事實，亦有欠公允」。

政府指出，委員會陳詞未釐清違規及監管責任的分野，望公眾理解事件涉及兩層責任，其一為直接責任，即導致火災蔓延及傷亡、私營持份者違法違規行為，另一層為監管制度弱點，即令違法行為未被即時發現的因素，但不等於直接導致火災的原因。

孫靖乾指，委員會大律師從事後角度審視部門決定，用結果去評斷事件時需要謹慎，因為最完善的法規都有可能發生事故。他續稱，相關制度設計和執行在大多數情況中有效運作，宏福苑屬於制度下極端、異常的情況，包括多個獲委任法定責任的承建商、專業人士蓄意忽略、違法、合謀、欺詐等。

他以屋宇署大火後修訂《註冊承建商作業備考》為例，新規定要求承建商採樣驗證棚網，工程時間和價格成本會相應增加，是大火後社會對承建商失去信心的決定，如在制度最初設計時實行同樣規定，或會引來業界質疑，最終成本轉嫁業主。孫靖乾以此反駁獨立委員會律師的說法，即委員會指欺詐行為因監管機構做法而成功，他指該說法有欠公允，因為欺詐的本質是繞過監管而行。

他再次強調，委員會應區分「直接導致火災因素」及「未能及時留意違法行為的監管空間」，兩者責任不應被放在同一天秤上，欺詐理應受委員會最強烈的譴責。政府認為，制度多年來在大多數情況下行之有效，但面對蓄意合謀、有組織欺詐時，便暴露出信任的弱點，並引述委員會陳詞指，政府信賴專業人士是各方合謀暪騙成功的原因，強調弱點不應等同火災直接成因。

另一方面，政府留意到事件涉及部門對規定的理解，同意可以做得更好，但不能抹煞分工的重要性，政府事後已全速檢視現行系統弱點、查找需要優化的地方，及時採取改善措施，並在上月中向委員會提交建議列表。孫靖乾形容，「政府態度可說是爭分奪秒，並非待委員會提出報告才採取改善措施」，包括昨日（17日）立法會通過地盤全面禁煙，明日（19日）生效。

孫靖乾其後兩小時，講述宏福苑大火背景、相關監管制度、各持份者角色，以及六項促成起火、火勢蔓延及造成重大傷亡的因素，包括工人在宏福苑工地範圍內吸煙、使用未經阻燃性能認證的棚網、發泡膠板封蓋窗戶、使用其他沒有阻燃性的建築物料、走火樓梯間開設「生口」令逃生失去防護、消防警鐘失效，力陳承辦商及顧問等私營持份者的作為及不作為。

斥承辦商及專業人士全面失責

政府午休後繼續陳詞，斥事件涉及承辦商及專業人士全面失責，違法行為涉及規避破壞現有制度框架，嚴重阻礙、削弱政府監管功能。孫靖乾指出，是次系統性濫用有兩個特點，其一為財務誘因規模巨大，宏福苑大維修工程造價約3.36億港元，現行罰則對比下實屬微不足道，濫用的收益遠高於風險。其二，專業人士選擇合謀而非互相監察，消防承辦商成虛假通知的「付費管道」，削弱監管架構保護公眾的作用。

緊急警示系統現已可分區使用

孫靖乾讚揚消防面對前所未有條件仍專業救火救援，充分體現消防人員精神和無私奉獻。政府同時承認，警方與消防使用傳真通訊做法不適合處理大規模事故，消防處已與警方聯合檢討訊息交流機制。孫亦指出，政府緊急警示系統（EAS）在大火時未被配置作地區性使用，亦缺乏公眾教育，目前EAS已改配置為可分區使用，並會設計公眾教育計劃配合。

五個系統性弱點

孫靖乾指出，政府坦誠面對制度、操作層面問題，綜合識別五個重點系統性弱點：

一、制度設計依賴專業人士自律，未足以防範蓄意合謀，本應監督的人員漠視職責，甚至成為共謀者，當局難發現違法濫用行為，可見自律模式不足以保障公眾；

二、部門經統計、抽樣審核不足以監察有組織欺騙手段，例如宏業選擇性更換棚網應付檢查，當局無法想像註冊檢驗人員、承建商會不斷欺騙政府；

三、程序指引及工作守則存在改善空間，火災前未有具體特定法例、工作守則或作業備考規管，例如臨時窗戶保護物料發泡膠、踢腳板等未有指定阻燃標準，令監管部門未有或難以採取果斷即時執法行動；

四、跨部門溝通機制存在弱點，情況可見於屋宇署與ICU內部溝通未及時傳達新巡查要求、警方與消防在緊急情況溝通有改善空間、欠缺統一跨部門機制處理投訴等等；

五、科技方面有滯後，在消防裝置監管、建築物料驗證、工地巡查地點選擇等各項情況有所體現。

然而，孫靖乾亦以英國格蘭菲爾大廈大火為例，指出即使有完善法規，都有可能發生事故，同樣教訓適用於宏福苑情況，整體而言，弱點在於沒有機制針對蓄意合謀或怠忽職守。政府已在今年6月15日向委員會提交「改善措施一覽表」，涵蓋七個範疇，分別針對消防裝置、建築物料、強制驗樓計劃及小型工程、專業人士、跨部門溝通、工地安全及科技作改善，希望可抵禦違法行為。

事先回應委員會法律團隊未公開的陳詞

獨立委員會法律團隊的聽證會總結尚未公開，孫靖乾陳詞時透露，政府留意到法律團隊總結對ICU、勞工處、消防處都有具體批評，因此希望提出三點澄清：

一、任何規管制度中，監管者某程度上皆需要倚賴受規管者提供訊息，強調宏福苑的情況涉及系統性顛覆，政府接受制度需要更有效驗證機制；

二、關於法律團隊批評多個政府部門收投訴後未有效跟進，政府希望委員會考慮部門有分工，並有各自專業範疇、管轄權限，政府已針對跨部門投訴落實改善措施；

三、法律團隊認為政府沒有任何部門能全面掌握宏福苑可預見火災風險，孫靖乾強調合理分工是有效行政系統的必要特徵，政府已推行多項跨部門措施，冀盡量改善制度弱點。

指「證據確立」專業人士濫用機制造成大火

孫靖乾最後總結政府陳詞，以「證據確立」四字形容承建商及專業人士於宏福苑的行為，認為聽證會眾多文件、證供皆顯示該些人士濫用旨在保護公眾的機制，辜負政府及市民的信任和期望，再次斥責涉事的私營持份者蓄意濫用機制、嚴重疏忽，造成大火。

他表示，政府坦承現行的監督架構需要加強監管程度，火災後亦行動迅速，於多個關鍵範疇檢討措施及做法，主動檢討措施，懇請委員會按認為適當的方式根據證據作出事實裁斷及建議，政府承諾會跟進，並再向因火災失去至親或家園的市民致以最深切慰問。

鄧炳強今日出席立法會會議後回應提問，他強調法例對煽動意圖定義清晰，「法例講得好清楚，你犯咗法就係僭越紅線，一犯法有證據我哋就拉，夠證據我哋就告。」他兩度被問及會否及曾否考慮設禁書名冊，他強調針對書籍內容而非書名，內容煽動憎恨政府、憎恨司法機構便會違法 。

鄧炳強指如果只列出書名的話，「好多人將一啲犯法，又或者有啲危害國家安全意圖嘅書改個書名。喔，你唔係黑名單喎，你拉我就唔得喎。咁我哋唔會係咁樣便宜嗰啲犯罪嘅人。」他以出售食物為例，表明書商有責任確保書籍不會國家安全，「你係賣食物嘅，你都確保你賣嘅食物都唔係會食到人哋肚痛、唔會係毒藥、唔會係違法呀，我相信作為書商有責任。」

有記者提及有書店被取消書展參展資格，問國安處是否有名單決定查那間書店。鄧炳強否認針對某一類型店鋪，指任何店鋪、個人危害國安、出售或展示有煽動意圖物品都會採取行動，不應將事件與同某一類別商店扯上關係。

此外，台灣總統賴清德回應事件指，「每一間獨立書店，都是守護思想的重要所在」。他提及香港多間獨立書店被搜查及相關人士被捕，指「香港的出版、閱讀與言論自由，正承受持續且嚴峻的壓力」。

賴清德指，書店是思想交會、保存社會記憶的重要空間。他指書籍可能成為罪證，書店被迫反覆揣測無形的紅線。「在這樣的壓力下，人民不再能自由地思考與表達，公共討論的空間也不斷被壓縮。」

他指台灣曾經歷查禁書刊、壓抑言論的戒嚴年代，深知民主自由得來不易，向在困境中堅守崗位的書店及文化工作者，表達關切與敬意。他重申，思想與文字，都不應因政治壓力而被禁錮。他期待香港社會的多元聲音、基本權利，獲得應有尊重與保障。

兩間獨立書店，留下書舍及田園書屋，昨日（15日）遭國安警上門搜查，及採取拘捕行動，據了解，留下書舍三人，及田園屋兩人，被指涉嫌干犯 23 條下的煽動罪被捕。

政府昨晚上十時許出稿指，警方國安處接獲海關轉介，調查後在旺角兩間書店拘捕五人，涉嫌違反《維護國家安全條例》第二十四條「出於煽動意圖作出具煽動意圖的作為」罪，並檢走一批書籍。

Apple's chip manufacturing partner TSMC had previously stated plans to build a total of eight fabrication plants in Arizona, and has now announced an expanded investment that could increase the number to as many as twelve.

This move may result in more chips used in Apple devices being produced in the United States, but there are reasons to remain skeptical about this possibility…

A TSMC chip fabrication plant in Arizona

Almost exactly one year ago today, TSMC announced it would accelerate construction of its second and third fabrication plants in Arizona. Apple was designated as the first customer for the third plant.

Some observers have questioned how much practical significance American chip production holds for Apple devices. One reason is that TSMC deliberately restricts its most advanced manufacturing processes to its fabs in its home country of Taiwan. The planned American plants are simply incapable of producing the chips needed for the latest Apple devices.

This means that only chips for older-model Apple devices—generally around three generations behind—can be produced in the United States. Even so, skepticism remains, because bare chips are only one step in the entire process. Apple's chips are actually composed of multiple different chips integrated through a procedure known as 'packaging,' and the original plan was to send the American-manufactured chips back to Taiwan for packaging.

One analyst therefore described the Arizona plant as nothing more than a 'paperweight.' There was briefly some discussion about entrusting packaging to a third-party American company, after which TSMC stated it would establish its own chip packaging facility in the United States.

Since then, the total number of planned American plants has increased to eight.

New investment may bring the number of American plants to twelve

The Trump administration has now announced that TSMC has agreed to an additional one hundred billion US dollars in investment in American facilities, claiming this will bring the total number of Arizona plants to twelve—though this figure includes both packaging and chip manufacturing facilities.

However, the picture TSMC itself paints is somewhat different. According to BBC News, TSMC has only stated that its expanded investment 'may' result in the construction of four new plants, and has not provided any timeline whatsoever.

Apple is also seeking partnerships with other chip manufacturers such as Intel and Samsung, which may further affect the 'market conditions' cited by TSMC when making this announcement.

In other words, this has all the hallmarks of a political announcement: promoting an eye-catching number for something that may or may not happen, without any timeline having been released.

從 Windows 轉用 Mac 幾乎沒有任何軟件上的限制。不單止所有最主流的電腦應用程式都可以在這個平台運行,還有數以百計的實用程式是 Mac 獨有的。

唯一的大例外是遊戲。不過,最新測試顯示,Windows 遊戲在 Mac 上的運行表現比以往更好,無論是官方還是非官方的方式運行都是這樣說……

Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you to possible high blood pressure, but they won't give you an actual reading.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but require periodic calibration with a traditional cuff blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to provide full blood pressure readings without any calibration, backed by clinical trials involving thousands of people…

「Silent Killer」

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) can both pose significant health risks.

Of the two, high blood pressure is more dangerous, hence known as the 「silent killer,」 because it can cause serious and irreversible damage to your arteries, heart, and brain without obvious symptoms. The condition often goes undetected until it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

For seniors, regular blood pressure monitoring is especially important, and home cuff-type blood pressure monitors are available on the market. However, being able to monitor automatically through a fitness device you already wear would certainly be the ideal approach.

Apple Watch blood pressure features

The launch of watchOS 26 has enabled five Apple Watch models to measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models won't give you any readings, but will alert you when possible signs of high blood pressure are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices can indeed provide actual blood pressure readings, but they require regular calibration with readings from a cuff blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup company Vital Signals has announced it has developed a smart ring, the Signal Ring, which claims to achieve measurement accuracy comparable to a traditional arm cuff blood pressure monitor without any calibration required.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Moss said he nearly died from an undiagnosed case of high blood pressure before founding the company.

The ring begins pre-ordering later today, ships in October, and is priced at US$399 with no subscription required. Real-time blood pressure readings and long-term tracking data can be displayed on the accompanying app (see image above).

It is worth noting that the Oura Ring has not yet been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials have shown that it can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss has no intention of selling this ring to everyone. He says these professional features are most suitable for seniors and people assessed by doctors as being at risk for high blood pressure, implicitly suggesting that the Signal Ring may not excel in other areas (such as sleep tracking).

While Apple's latest price hike for Mac and iPad AppleCare+ may seem modest on its own, it has made AppleCare One's value proposition even more compelling. Apple has also raised the hardware pricing for Mac and iPad, making consumers more inclined to seriously consider protection plans.

AppleCare One's pricing remains unchanged for now

All new standalone AppleCare+ subscriptions for current Mac and iPad models are increasing by US$0.50 per month or US$5 per year; existing subscribers will continue to enjoy their original pricing.

On the other hand, AppleCare One's monthly fee remains at US$19.99, covering up to three devices.

The standalone monthly protection plan for the 13-inch MacBook Air is now US$7.99, for the 11-inch iPad Air is US$6.99, and for the iPhone 17 Pro with theft and loss coverage is US$13.99. The three plans combined cost US$28.97 per month; AppleCare One covers all three devices for just US$19.99, saving US$8.98 per month, or US$107.76 over 12 months.

Apple offers discounts on standalone annual plans, so comparing them on an annual basis is fairer: the MacBook Air is US$79.99, the iPad Air is US$69.99, and the iPhone 17 Pro is US$139.99, totaling US$289.97; while AppleCare One's 12-month cost is US$239.88, the gap remains considerable at US$50.09.

The savings with AppleCare One are even more significant on higher-end Mac and iPad models.

The monthly AppleCare+ fee for the 16-inch MacBook Pro has been raised to US$15.99, while the protection plan for the 13-inch iPad Pro is US$11.99, totaling US$27.98 combined. In other words, users using just two of their AppleCare One slots can already save US$7.99 per month compared to standalone subscriptions.

AppleCare One has just reached its one-year anniversary

Apple announced AppleCare One on July 23, 2025, and officially launched it in the United States the following day. The basic subscription covers up to three eligible Apple products, with each additional device requiring an extra US$5.99 per month.

The plan includes the core protections of AppleCare+: unlimited accidental damage repairs (subject to a service fee), battery service, 24/7 priority support, and repairs by Apple-certified technicians.

The plan also covers theft and loss protection for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch, with a combined maximum of three claims per year.

Eligible products up to four years old can be added to the plan, provided they pass Apple's condition check, rather than being limited to the standard AppleCare+ purchase window.

Devices can be added to or removed from the plan at any time; when a covered product is traded in directly to Apple, the coverage is automatically replaced.

AppleCare One may not be the best value for every product combination. For example, buying standalone protection for just a MacBook Air and an iPad Air costs only US$14.98 per month. However, anyone needing to insure three products, or who owns both a high-end Mac and iPad, should definitely run the numbers again.

With standalone protection plans getting more expensive while AppleCare One remains at its original price, this bundled subscription has become one of Apple's more generous offerings.

As I mentioned, this is my personal favorite of the bunch because of how versatile it is. It's compact, solidly built, has most of the main ports people need, and works with multiple devices.

The OntheGo Multiport Adapter is available in the same colors as the MacBook Neo, and is now on sale at Amazon and the Satechi website for $44.99.

This one is the familiar, more traditional USB-C hub form factor. It magnetically attaches to the side of the MacBook Neo (hence the name "Snap hub"), expanding it with six new ports—one more than the OntheGo hub above. From how securely it attaches, you can tell it's designed specifically for the MacBook Neo. The ports the Snap Hub provides include:

  • SD and MicroSD card readers
  • USB-C pass-through charging up to 45W (plenty to charge the MacBook Neo, since the Neo caps at 30W)

The Snap Hub is undoubtedly the most visually integrated of the three accessories. It looks and feels like something Apple themselves would have made. It uses a two-tone design, with the top perfectly matching the MacBook Neo's material and color, but the surrounding housing cleverly uses a soft-touch rubber material because they know this is the part that will sit right up against the MacBook Neo's metal body, and metal on metal contact doesn't usually work well. I think that's an excellent design decision. One thing to note is that this hub will take up two of the MacBook Neo's USB-C ports, but the hub itself still provides two USB-C ports plus additional

The USB-C Snap Hub is now available in the four MacBook Neo colors mentioned above, also priced at $44.99, and is available on Amazon and the Satechi website.

As the grand finale of Satechi's new MacBook Neo lineup, they've redesigned the Slim EX mouse in colors that match the entire product range. I previously tested the non-color version of this mouse, and thanks to its value, it became one of the most recommended products. For just $29, you get:

  • Connect up to 3 different devices simultaneously: two via Bluetooth, one via a 2.4GHz receiver (and it's a USB-C receiver!)
  • Aluminum body
  • Charges via USB-C
  • Replaceable battery
  • Up to three months of use, with standby mode lasting over a year
  • A USB-C cable is also included for charging and connection

This mouse is built and feels like a mouse that costs twice as much. It has a slim aluminum body that's ergonomic even during extended use. The ability to quickly switch between multiple devices is incredibly practical for me, as I often switch back and forth between my MacBook and iPad. Additionally, the 2.4GHz receiver uses USB-C instead of USB-A, which is a seriously underrated upgrade. Even though the MacBook Neo's trackpad is already excellent, I personally still like using both a trackpad and a mouse. The trackpad for gestures and horizontal scrolling, and the mouse for more precise operations.

The Slim EX wireless mouse is available in the four colors mentioned above, as well as the previously released black version. The mouse is priced at $29.99 and is available on Amazon and the Satechi website. If you want to save some money, the black version has exactly the same features and is currently on sale for $23.99.

Summary

Satechi is the first company to launch accessories in matching original colors for the MacBook Neo, and they clearly understand their target audience well. They've brought high-quality, practical accessories to the MacBook Neo lineup, making up for the tradeoffs that come with this $699 laptop. All of these accessories are well-made, offer plenty of practical features, and enhance the MacBook Neo experience.

If I had to pick one of these products, I'd lean slightly toward the OntheGo Multiport Adapter, purely because of its versatility and the fact that it works with any device that has USB-C and MagSafe. However, the Snap Hub is also excellent, with an extremely high level of physical integration with the MacBook Neo, and the Slim EX mouse is the perfect finishing touch to the whole package. A California Apple user has filed a class action lawsuit in court, accusing the company of misleading customers about the privacy protections of its "Hide My Email" feature. The details are as follows.

Apple sued over alleged 'Hide My Email' flaw

Recently, 404 Media reported that Apple had been aware of a so-called vulnerability for over a year that could expose the real email address behind a "Hide My Email" alias.

Apple's "Hide My Email" feature allows users to create unique, randomly generated email addresses that forward messages to their personal inbox, so they don't have to disclose their real address when signing up for apps, websites, and newsletters.

This feature is available for free through "Sign in with Apple"; a more comprehensive version, included with the iCloud+ plan (starting at $0.99 per month), lets users create aliases for websites, newsletters, and other services.

According to 404 Media, a security researcher notified Apple of the vulnerability in June 2025, which could expose the real email address behind a "Hide My Email" alias.

Apple confirmed receipt of the report about a month later, but allegedly failed to fix the issue. In March 2026, the company said it had patched the vulnerability, but the researcher found it could still be exploited.

The following is excerpted from 404 Media:

Speaking of the lawsuit (reported by MacRumors), plaintiff Anthony Alvarez said:

Apple has been aware of the issue for over a year and still has not fixed the flaw—yet Apple continues to profit from "Hide My Email" and its privacy promises. The plaintiff is one of millions of customers who pay Apple for iCloud+ and rely on Apple's claim that "Hide My Email" protects their personal email addresses from being exposed. Plaintiffs and class members pay Apple for privacy—iCloud+ subscribers through a premium in the iCloud+ subscription fee, and all Apple customers through a premium in the price of Apple products, because Apple markets its products as equipped with enhanced privacy protections and features including "Hide My Email".

The lawsuit also claims this is not an isolated incident, citing a 2023 report that Apple's MAC address randomization feature could expose users' real hardware identification codes.

The lawsuit also alleges that the total amount sought by the proposed class members exceeds $5 million (excluding interest and costs), but does not explain how that figure was calculated.

Alvarez filed the lawsuit on behalf of himself and other Apple customers he claims were similarly affected. He is asking the court to certify the case as a class action, covering four proposed user groups:

  • A nationwide group of Apple customers who purchased devices and used "Hide My Email";
  • A California subset of the above users;
  • A nationwide group of iCloud+ subscribers who have used the feature;
  • A California subset of iCloud+ subscribers.

He is demanding a jury trial and, in addition to monetary damages in an amount to be determined, is asking the court to order Apple to fix "Hide My Email" or clearly disclose its limitations.

Apple has not yet responded to the lawsuit.

作為重溫，AutoMix 利用人工智能在 Apple Music 歌曲之間創造如 DJ 般的過場效果。據 Apple 稱，初版功能採用了「時間拉伸及節拍匹配」等技術，以達致完美過渡。

我很享受 Apple Music 如何從一首歌過渡到另一首，尤其是風格截然不同的歌曲之間。它為聆聽體驗增添了一份趣味新意。
